docs.searchField.a11y.disabled: Disabled and read-only are different. A disabled field leaves the tab order and is not sent; a read-only one keeps the focus and its value can be read, selected and sent, and its dashed border says it cannot be changed.
docs.searchField.a11y.escape: Escape clears a field that has text and goes no further, so a search box inside a dialog or a popover empties first, and only a second Escape reaches what closes it. On an empty or read-only field it does nothing and the key goes on. The focus stays in the field.
docs.searchField.a11y.focus: The focus ring is the one of Input: it shows with the keyboard and is never removed. The magnifier ignores the pointer, so a click on it focuses the field.
docs.searchField.a11y.icon: The magnifier is decorative: it is hidden from screen readers and carries nothing that the label does not already say.
docs.searchField.a11y.label: The label names the field for assistive technology and is not drawn: a sighted person reads the magnifier, the placeholder and the page around it. Use it where the page already says what is searched. If the field needs a visible label, use Input.
docs.searchField.a11y.native: It is a native input type="search", so a screen reader announces a search box and the behavior of the browser stays: the text can be selected, a form sends it and it can be autofilled. The library adds the magnifier and the Escape key.
docs.searchField.a11y.strings: SearchField has no text of its own: the label and the placeholder are yours, in the language of your page, and a FormaProvider changes nothing here. The clear button of the browser, whose text follows the language of the browser and not the one of your page, is hidden.
docs.searchField.api.className: Added to the input, after the library's own class names.
docs.searchField.api.fieldClassName: Class name of the container of the field. className goes to the input.
docs.searchField.api.id: Native: the label points at it. One is generated when you leave it out.
docs.searchField.api.label: The accessible name of the field. It is not drawn: screen readers read it, and sighted people read the magnifier and the placeholder.
docs.searchField.api.onKeyDown: Native: called after the field handles Escape, whether it cleared the text or not.
docs.searchField.api.onValueChange: Called with the whole new text when the person types, pastes or clears the field, and with an empty string when Escape clears it.
docs.searchField.api.others: Every other attribute of the native input element goes to it as it is: name, placeholder, disabled, autoComplete, aria-*, the event handlers and ref. It takes no type, which is always search, no onChange, which is onValueChange, and no children.
docs.searchField.api.readOnly: Native: a read-only field keeps its text when Escape is pressed.
docs.searchField.api.value: The text of the field. It is required: the field is always controlled.
docs.searchField.controlled.description: The field has no state of its own: value is what it shows, and onValueChange is how it asks to change. Because the parent owns the text, it can read it, filter a list with it or refuse a change.
docs.searchField.controlled.hint: The line under the field reads the state of the parent.
docs.searchField.controlled.title: Controlled
docs.searchField.limit.clear: The clear button of the browser is hidden, since Escape clears the field the same way in every browser. A person with a pointer has no button to clear it: put an IconButton beside the field if the layout needs one.
docs.searchField.limit.controlled: It is always controlled: value and onValueChange are required, and there is no defaultValue. The field shows the text you give it and nothing else.
docs.searchField.limit.design: The box is the one of Input, so it is painted on the surface color and has the hover and the states of Input. In Resolve, where the component comes from, the field is on the page color: whether to keep that difference is a pending design decision.
docs.searchField.limit.hint: It takes no hint and no error: its box is the one of Input, but it is a search box, not a form field. Use Input when the field needs either.
docs.searchField.limit.results: It only collects the text. It does not debounce, search, suggest or say how many results there are: do that in your component, and announce the count in a live region.
docs.searchField.limit.size: There is one size: 40 px high, and 44 px below 768 px of width, with a 20 px magnifier.
docs.searchField.state.defaultHint: Empty: the placeholder shows, and Escape does nothing.
docs.searchField.state.disabledHint: It is not focusable and a form does not send its value.
docs.searchField.state.readOnlyHint: It takes the focus and a form sends its value, but Escape does not clear it.
docs.searchField.state.valueHint: With text: Escape clears it, and the focus stays in the field.
docs.searchField.states.description: The states that SearchField has today. Disabled and read-only are two different states: they look and behave in different ways. Every field here keeps its own text: type in it, then press Escape.
docs.searchField.summary: A search box on a native search input, with a magnifier. Its label names it for screen readers and is not drawn.
docs.searchField.usage.description: Import SearchField and give it a label, a value and an onValueChange: the text lives in your component, and the field shows what you give it. The label is not drawn, so the page has to say what is searched.
